raw_review_excerpt:
The advisory's directional call is sound: reconciliation-first, no blind overwrite, repo-local authority for fork-specific rules. However, the proposed two-layer mechanism (generic skill + per-repo manifest with 8+ fields) is overengineered for a two-repo problem and does not address the empirically verified root cause of Archon skill drift — a static-import bundler that silently omits new files. Two focused repo-local procedures would deliver the same safety with fewer artifacts and no new abstraction layer.

Issues:
- 1. [WARN] YAGNI: generic skill + manifest schema at N=2
- 2. [WARN] Bundle drift root cause is not addressed by governance
- 3. [WARN] Manifest duplicates operating guide, creating a new drift surface
- 4. [NOTE] Three-surface ambiguity for Archon not resolved
- 5. [NOTE] Unverified assumption that global install is needed

issues.title: YAGNI: generic skill + manifest schema at N=2
issues.details: The recommendation introduces a generic my-fork-skill-sync skill with an 8-field manifest schema, classification taxonomy (port/adapt/preserve/drop/defer), and per-repo operating guides — all for exactly two repos. The coding contract says 'generalize only when there is a demonstrated second use case.' Two is the threshold to consider extraction, not a mandate to build a framework. Two short repo-local sync procedures would deliver identical safety with fewer artifacts and no new abstraction.
issues.suggested_fix: Before building the generic skill, demonstrate that two independent repo-local procedures (one Archon, one Graphify) would fail to catch a real conflict that the generic engine would catch. If no such case exists, ship the repo-local procedures first and defer the generic layer.

issues.title: Bundle drift root cause is not addressed by governance
issues.details: The empirically verified problem — bundled-skill.ts silently omits codex-workflow-status.md (confirmed: 26 files in the map vs 27+ in .agents/skills/archon/) — is a build-time enumeration bug. No manifest, sync skill, or governance pattern fixes it. The advisory recommends installing globally 'after fixing the bundled-skill drift' but treats the two as separable steps, when the bundle mechanism is the primary drift vector for Archon.
issues.suggested_fix: Fix the bundle drift first: add a build-time or CI check that enumerates .agents/skills/archon/**/*.md and fails when the set disagrees with BUNDLED_SKILL_FILES keys. This is a prerequisite for any governance pattern, not a parallel workstream.

issues.title: Manifest duplicates operating guide, creating a new drift surface
issues.details: The proposal calls for per-repo manifests listing source paths, global paths, CLI verifier commands, protected paths, and sync modes. The repo-local operating guides (my-achrchon-sync/SKILL.md already has protected paths; Graphify allegedly has mase-fork-operating-model.md) contain the same facts. Two sources of truth for the same facts is the exact drift the advisory claims to prevent.
issues.suggested_fix: If a machine-readable manifest is needed, generate it from the operating guide or consolidate into one surface. Do not maintain parallel human-authored documents with overlapping facts.

issues.title: Three-surface ambiguity for Archon not resolved
issues.details: Archon has four skill surfaces: .agents/skills/archon/ (authored source), .claude/skills/archon/ (byte-identical mirror), BUNDLED_SKILL_FILES (compile-time snapshot), and potentially /Users/mase/.codex/skills/archon/ (global install). The advisory acknowledges the .agents↔.claude mirror but doesn't define which surface is canonical input for the bundle or the global install, or what happens when .agents and .claude diverge.
issues.suggested_fix: Define the canonical chain explicitly: .agents/ is source → .claude/ is derived mirror → bundle is compile-time snapshot of .agents/ → global install is deployment copy of bundle output. Then verify the existing mirror and bundle mechanisms enforce this chain.

issues.title: Unverified assumption that global install is needed
issues.details: The advisory recommends installing the Archon host skill globally 'for convenience' but the current setup (bun symlink into local fork, archon version reporting source build) already works. No justification is given for why a separate global skill copy is needed when the CLI is already locally linked.
issues.suggested_fix: Document a concrete use case where the global Codex skill copy provides value that the local fork + bun symlink does not, before recommending the global install path.

review.best_case: The directional principles are correct and durable: reconciliation-first, no blind overwrite, repo-local authority for fork-specific rules, explicit approval before any write. If adopted with the right sizing — two focused repo-local procedures instead of a generic engine — this pattern prevents the class of silent-overwrite bugs that skill sync is prone to, while staying maintainable at Mase's actual scale of two repos.
strongest_objections: YAGNI: the two-layer pattern (generic skill + manifest + operating guide) is a framework for two repos. Two independent repo-local procedures deliver the same safety with fewer artifacts and no new abstraction to maintain.

Root cause mismatch: Archon's verified drift problem is a static-import bundler that silently omits files. No governance pattern, manifest, or sync skill addresses this — only a build-time enumeration check does. The advisory treats bundle-fixing and governance as separable when they aren't.

Manifest-guide duplication: the proposed manifest contains facts already in existing operating guides (protected paths, CLI verifiers, sync direction). Two human-authored surfaces for the same facts creates the drift the pattern claims to prevent.

Sync-direction asymmetry: Graphify ships through a CLI package mechanism; Archon ships through compile-time static imports. A generic skill abstracting both either becomes lowest-common-denominator (just diff + approve) or grows per-repo branches — at which point repo-local procedures are simpler.
Undemonstrated need for global install: the advisory recommends installing Archon's host skill globally 'for convenience' without showing that the existing bun-symlink setup is insufficient.
hidden_assumptions: That Mase regularly edits the global skill copies directly. If 95%+ of edits go to repo source, the heavyweight bidirectional reconciliation pattern is solving a rare case.
That 'latest' is genuinely hard to determine. For a single-developer fork with git history on both sides, git log comparison may be sufficient without a classification taxonomy.
That the manifest will stay in sync with operating guides. The pattern introduces a new maintenance surface while claiming to reduce drift.

That a generic skill engine provides value over a checklist. The proposed skill's core behavior (diff, show git history, propose patches, require approval) is operationally identical to a documented manual procedure.
That Archon should be globally installed at all. The advisory assumes this without justifying why the local fork symlink is insufficient.
review.what_would_change_my_mind: A demonstrated real-world case where a generic sync engine caught a conflict that two independent repo-local procedures would have missed. Or: evidence that the manifest format is consumed by a machine validator (CI check, doctor command, build-time verifier) rather than being a human-read document — that would justify it as a separate artifact from the operating guide. Or: evidence that Mase edits global skill copies frequently enough that the bidirectional reconciliation pattern is the common case rather than an edge case.
